coverage.qualification: Edition overview and exact 8.8 matrices distinguish Essentials Cloud and Premier Cloud/Cloud Connected, license, regional exception and enablement. The Security AI Assistant is separate from standalone SAIA. A supported deployment alone does not qualify each regional feature. 8.8 aggregate lists both editions, Cloud Platform 10.1.x+ and CMP Platform 10.4.x+/ES 8.8+/Cloud Connect 2.0+. Linked 8.8 task also states ES 8.6+ in Cloud and requires finding-based detections off. Where the Cloud Connected setup is used, independently read SAIA 2.4 installer and retain license, network/certificate, fresh-setup and commercial-region conditions. The aggregate lists both Cloud editions. The linked 8.8 SOP guide lists DOCX, MD, PDF, TXT and ZIP in its initial upload list, but its own Considerations omit ZIP. Security AI Assistant enablement, response-template view/edit permissions and human review remain explicit. Actual ZIP upload behavior is unresolved. 8.8 product is GA but the Threat Graph feature is Alpha, Premier Cloud, ES 8.8 or higher and representative enablement. The linked guide requires an enabled risk-based detection and about a million processed events before any findings, then distinguishes test queue routing. Current 8.8 table lists Premier Triage Cloud/CMP and separate Controlled Availability Response. The Response availability column says Cloud only while the adjacent compatibility text includes CMP requirements. The 8.8 parent documents per-tenant analysis and investigation revision limits. Detailed Cloud and CMP installation, representative enablement, paired SOAR, approved model and connector/asset permissions remain separately scoped. Both public origins omit the documented Threat Graph event-volume gate in the tested reader answer. The corrected AI and Editions candidate needs release acceptance and public retest.

coverage.qualification: ES 8.8 licensing separates the underlying Splunk platform license and ES use of ingested data. ES adds no ingestion. Representative-issued trials are 30 days for Essentials and 90 days for Premier; an existing Essentials customer reverts to the purchased entitlement without losing previously processed data. Cloud Connected features continue during an active Premier trial while the UI displays Essentials because Splunk Cloud Services does not recognize trial entitlements. Source also distinguishes trial-expiration UI behavior in a search head cluster and feature blocks at expiry. The edition overview places native SOAR and native UEBA in Premier; the public pricing table keeps pricing models and standalone SOAR distinct from any entitlement determination. The freshly read pricing-model FAQ names activity-based pricing for Splunk Cloud Platform. The ES pricing summary includes it, but does not establish ES-specific customer-managed eligibility. The existing public Editions licensing block lacks the Cloud Connected trial entitlement explanation. The candidate supplies it and keeps the trial limits.

assessments.evidence: Current 8.8 Agentic offerings list Guided Response for Essentials and Premier on Cloud and Cloud Connected CMP, ES 8.6+ and a paired SOAR instance, while the 8.8 Cloud capability matrix describes the 8.7 Premier enhancement. The same aggregate lists Connector Builder for both Cloud editions, while the freshly reread 8.7.1 release row says Premier for eligible users. Automation Builder guide requires Cloud Platform 10.1+, paired SOAR Cloud with ES 8.6+, account and permission, and excludes its FedRAMP stacks. UEBA FAQ calls native UEBA Premier-only and explicitly excludes a standalone offering or Essentials add-on. App for SOAR 8.8.0 published on-premises compatibility cell literally says 8..0.
